q: In a pit line provided in a coaching yard under a yard work, an examination pit is constructed between and alongside the rails. The examination pit enables the staff to:

options.A: Store the tools used in the yard
options.B: Drain the washings from the coaches
options.C: Go below the coaches standing on the line and examine and attend to their undergear
options.D: Board the coaches for ticket checking

q: A traverser is provided in a workshop or yard layout executed under a work. A traverser is a device by which:

options.A: A wagon is lifted bodily for changing its bogies
options.B: A locomotive is turned to face the opposite direction
options.C: Water is supplied to locomotives in the yard
options.D: A vehicle standing on a track is shifted laterally, on a moving platform, to a parallel track

q: In the layout of a station yard executed under a work, 'isolation' of the running lines from the siding lines is provided. Isolation in this context means an arrangement by which:

options.A: Vehicles standing or moving in a siding cannot foul or come in the way of movements on the running line, and conflicting movements are prevented
options.B: The siding is kept locked and is never used for traffic
options.C: The running line is separated from the siding by a high fence
options.D: Only one train is allowed in the station at a time

q: A sharp curve falls on a rising gradient of a section and, in the alignment adopted for the work, the gradient on the curved portion is kept flatter than the ruling gradient of the section. The gradient is so compensated on the curve because:

options.A: Trains run faster on curves than on the straight
options.B: A curve offers additional resistance to the movement of trains, which is allowed for by easing the gradient on the curved portion
options.C: The rails on a curve are shorter than on the straight
options.D: The sleepers on a curve require a flatter bed

q: The treads of the wheels of rolling stock are not flat but are given a coned profile. The coning of wheels serves principally to:

options.A: Reduce the weight of the wheelset
options.B: Make the wheels run silently on the track
options.C: Enable the wheelset to shift laterally on curves so that the outer wheel rolls on a larger radius than the inner wheel, helping the vehicle negotiate the curve
options.D: Prevent the wheels from being braked on gradients

q: In a works contract, the stipulation that 'time is of the essence of the contract' signifies that:

options.A: The contractor may complete the work at any time convenient to him
options.B: Completion of the work within the stipulated period is an essential term of the contract, failure of which entitles the Railway to the remedies provided for delay and default
options.C: The period of completion can be extended only by the Railway Board
options.D: Liquidated damages cannot be levied for delay in completion

q: 'Repudiation' of a works contract by the contractor takes place when the contractor:

options.A: Declares, by words or conduct, that he will not perform his obligations under the contract, before the time fixed for performance
options.B: Completes the work after the stipulated date of completion
options.C: Applies for extension of the period of completion
options.D: Claims payment for an extra item of work executed by him

q: A tenderer participates in a tender without protest and, after his tender is rejected, challenges the very tender condition under which he had participated. In tender matters, such a challenge is ordinarily not entertained on the principle of:

options.A: Res judicata
options.B: Subrogation
options.C: Estoppel, a party who has accepted and acted under the conditions being barred from questioning them afterwards
options.D: Force majeure

q: The 'severability' provision in a contract means that:

options.A: The contract can be assigned by the contractor in parts
options.B: The Railway may terminate the contract in parts at its convenience
options.C: Payments under the contract are made in severable instalments
options.D: If any one provision of the contract is held invalid, the remaining provisions continue to remain valid and enforceable

q: In works execution, payment on a 'daywork' basis means payment:

options.A: For the actual labour, materials and plant deployed on the work each day, at the rates provided for the purpose, adopted where the work cannot be conveniently measured and paid for by quantity
options.B: Of wages to departmental labour engaged on the work
options.C: Made to the contractor in advance at the start of each day's work
options.D: For work executed only during the daytime

q: A 'through rate' quoted or analysed for an item of supply-cum-work, such as supply of ballast, is a rate which:

options.A: Covers only the cost of the material at the source of supply
options.B: Covers only the railway freight for carriage of the material
options.C: Is complete in all respects, covering the cost of the material and all operations such as loading, carriage, unloading and stacking at the required place
options.D: Is provisional and is revised after every running bill

q: In the analysis of rates for a work, 'cartage' refers to:

options.A: The hire charges of tools and plant used on the work
options.B: The cost of conveying materials by road over a short distance, such as from the place of stacking or supply to the site of the work
options.C: The royalty payable on minor minerals consumed in the work
options.D: The departmental charges levied on the work

q: A 'non-scheduled item' in the schedule of a works tender is an item which:

options.A: Is ordered during execution in place of an item of the original contract
options.B: Is an item of the contractor's own tools and plant
options.C: Can be executed by the contractor without any rate being payable for it
options.D: Is not covered by the applicable schedule of rates, and is provided in the tender schedule itself with a rate derived from analysis or market rates

q: Where water and electricity required by a works contractor for construction purposes are supplied by the Railway from its own sources, the position under the contract is that:

options.A: The cost thereof is recovered from the contractor's bills at the rates prescribed for the purpose
options.B: They are supplied free of cost in all cases
options.C: The contractor is required to pay for them only after the final bill is settled
options.D: No accountal of such supplies is necessary

q: In preparing the estimate of a renewal or dismantling work, serviceable materials expected to be released from the existing structure are dealt with by:

options.A: Ignoring their value altogether in the estimate
options.B: Providing for a credit to the work for the salvage value of the materials so released
options.C: Charging their original cost again to the estimate of the new work
options.D: Treating them as the property of the contractor executing the work

q: Before surplus or unserviceable materials released from a work are sold by auction, an 'upset price' (reserve price) is fixed in order that:

options.A: The materials are necessarily sold below their book value
options.B: The auction is dispensed with and the materials are sold by negotiation
options.C: The materials are not sold below that price without the approval of the competent authority
options.D: The purchaser is required to deposit the full book value in advance

q: Under the conditions of a works contract, the contractor is required to maintain at the site of the work, for superintendence of the work:

options.A: A representative of the tender committee
options.B: An officer deputed by the Railway Accounts department
options.C: Only unskilled labour for receiving instructions of the Engineer
options.D: A competent representative or agent, approved by the Engineer, who is authorised to receive instructions and directions on behalf of the contractor

q: A performance guarantee furnished by a contractor in the form of a bank guarantee is valid only up to a specified date, while the work is still incomplete. In such a situation:

options.A: The guarantee is automatically treated as extended till completion
options.B: The contractor is required to get its validity extended before its expiry, failing which the Railway may proceed to encash it before it lapses
options.C: The Railway has no remedy and must wait till the work is completed
options.D: The earnest money of the contractor is forfeited in lieu of the guarantee

q: The financial eligibility criteria prescribed in a works tender, relating to the annual turnover of the tenderer, are intended to ensure that:

options.A: The tenderer has the financial capacity and resources commensurate with the value of the work tendered for
options.B: The tenderer has executed the same work earlier for the Railways
options.C: The tenderer is registered with the Registrar of Companies
options.D: The tenderer maintains an office in the division where the work lies

q: The 'available bid capacity' of a tenderer, assessed at the time of evaluation of a works tender, represents:

options.A: The total value of all works the tenderer has executed since his enlistment
options.B: The value of the earnest money the tenderer can deposit
options.C: The capacity of the tenderer to take up additional work, assessed after taking into account the value of the works already in hand with him and his assessed capacity
options.D: The maximum value of bank guarantee the tenderer's bank can issue

q: An officer who is a member of a tender committee for a work has a personal or financial interest in one of the tendering firms. The correct course for such an officer is to:

options.A: Participate in the deliberations but abstain from signing the recommendations
options.B: Recommend the tender of that firm if it happens to be the lowest
options.C: Decide the tender himself as the accepting authority
options.D: Disclose the interest and not take part in the consideration of that tender

q: Notices and communications required to be served on a contractor under a works contract are ordinarily treated as duly served when they are:

options.A: Communicated orally to any workman present at the site
options.B: Sent in writing to the contractor at the address given by him for the purpose, in the manner provided in the contract
options.C: Published in a local newspaper
options.D: Pasted on the notice board of the Railway station nearest to the site

q: Where payment for supplies or services received from a micro or small enterprise is delayed beyond the period provided under the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, the buyer is liable to pay:

options.A: Interest on the delayed payment at the rate provided under that Act
options.B: Liquidated damages to the enterprise at the contract rate
options.C: Only the principal amount, whenever funds become available
options.D: A penalty to the Government equal to the amount delayed

q: Disputes relating to delayed payments to micro and small enterprises are referred for resolution to:

options.A: The arbitral tribunal appointed under the works contract
options.B: The tender committee which awarded the work
options.C: The Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council, including through the Samadhaan portal
options.D: The Central Administrative Tribunal

q: On the Government e-Marketplace, an 'incident' raised by a buyer against a seller relates to matters such as:

options.A: Registration of a new buyer on the portal
options.B: Non-supply, delayed supply or supply of goods or services not conforming to the order, on the basis of which action as provided on the portal may follow against the seller
options.C: Revision of the catalogue price by the seller
options.D: Selection of the payment authority for the order

q: In a 'time-based' consultancy contract, the consultant is remunerated:

options.A: By a fixed lump sum for the whole assignment, irrespective of the time taken
options.B: Only after the entire project designed by him is commissioned
options.C: By a percentage of the cost of the work designed by him in all cases
options.D: On the basis of the time actually spent by his personnel on the assignment, at the agreed rates, together with reimbursable expenses as provided

q: Repetitive buildings of the Railways, such as staff quarters, are ordinarily constructed to approved 'type designs' principally in order to:

options.A: Ensure uniformity of design and standards and economy in the preparation of designs and estimates
options.B: Enable every division to adopt a different design for each quarter
options.C: Dispense with the sanction of estimates for such buildings
options.D: Permit the contractor to alter the design at his discretion

q: Departmental materials issued to a works contractor are found to have been wasted in handling and use at the site well beyond the permissible limits. The cost of the wastage beyond the permissible limit is:

options.A: Borne by the Railways as a normal works expense
options.B: Written off automatically at the close of the work
options.C: Recoverable from the contractor
options.D: Adjusted against the contingencies provided in the estimate

q: Cement which has been stored at the site of a work for a long period is proposed to be used in an important work. Before such cement is used, it should be:

options.A: Used straightaway, as cement does not deteriorate in storage
options.B: Tested to ascertain that it still conforms to the required standard of strength and quality
options.C: Issued only for unimportant works without any check
options.D: Returned to the stores depot in every case

q: The 'seat' of arbitration specified in connection with a contract dispute is significant principally because:

options.A: It determines the courts which will have jurisdiction over the arbitral proceedings, including applications in connection with the award
options.B: It fixes the fees payable to the arbitrators
options.C: It decides the number of arbitrators to be appointed
options.D: It bars the contractor from demanding arbitration altogether

q: The facility of taking a pipeline or cable across railway land under a way-leave arrangement is, in its legal nature, in the nature of an easement because:

options.A: Ownership of the railway land is transferred to the party
options.B: The party acquires a permanent tenancy over the land
options.C: The arrangement can never be terminated by the Railways
options.D: The party is permitted a specific use of the land, such as passage of its pipeline or cable, without acquiring ownership of the land itself

q: In the estimate of a major project, the shifting of utilities, such as cables, pipelines and other services which fall in the alignment of the work, is dealt with by:

options.A: Leaving it to be arranged by the contractor at his own cost in every case
options.B: Ignoring it, as utilities are never shifted for a project
options.C: Making provision for the cost of such shifting in the project estimate, so that the work is not held up on that account
options.D: Charging it to the contingencies of an unrelated work

q: The tax deducted at source from the bills of a works contractor under the Income-tax Act is:

options.A: Treated as an earning of the Railways
options.B: Deposited with the Central Government, and the contractor is given credit for it in his tax assessment, supported by the tax deduction certificate or statement
options.C: Retained in the Material-at-Site account of the work
options.D: Refunded to the contractor along with his final bill

q: Tax deduction at source under the Goods and Services Tax law, where applicable to a payment made by the Railways to a works contractor, operates so that:

options.A: The amount so deducted is deposited with the Government and is available to the contractor as credit in his electronic cash ledger, as reflected in his returns
options.B: The amount deducted becomes a part of the security deposit of the contractor
options.C: The contractor is exempted from filing any return for that period
options.D: The deduction is made only from the final bill of the work

q: Contractors' bills on the Railways are, as a rule, subjected to internal check by the Accounts office before payment. This system is known as:

options.A: Post-check of bills
options.B: Test audit of bills
options.C: Concurrent audit of bills
options.D: Pre-check of bills

q: Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an arbitral award is ordinarily required to be a 'reasoned' or speaking award, which means that:

options.A: The award must record only the operative directions, without any findings
options.B: The award must be announced orally at a public hearing
options.C: The award must state the reasons on which it is based, unless the parties have agreed that no reasons are to be given or it records a settlement on agreed terms
options.D: The reasons for the award are recorded separately and are never supplied to the parties

q: In an Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) contract, payments to the contractor are ordinarily linked to:

options.A: The completion of the stages or milestones of the work specified in the contract, rather than to item-wise measurements of quantities
options.B: The measurements recorded item-wise in the Measurement Book for every item
options.C: The monthly establishment charges of the contractor
options.D: The value of materials stocked by the contractor at the site

q: A works contractor is allotted railway land near the site purely for stacking his materials and putting up his temporary site facilities for the duration of the work. For such occupation of railway land, the contractor is liable to pay:

options.A: The cost of acquisition of the land
options.B: Departmental charges on the estimated cost of the work
options.C: Nothing, as the land is allotted for the Railway's own work
options.D: Licence fee or ground rent for the land so occupied, as provided in the contract or the applicable rules

q: Before passing the bills of a contractor who engages labour on a work, the submission of proof of deposit of the provident fund and employees' state insurance contributions for his labour is insisted upon principally in order to:

options.A: Enable the Railways to recover the contributions as its own earnings
options.B: Ensure that the contractor has discharged his statutory obligations towards the labour engaged by him, for which the Railway can otherwise be held liable as principal employer
options.C: Decide the rates payable for the items of the work
options.D: Verify the measurements recorded in the Measurement Book

q: Service contracts arranged through the Government e-Marketplace ordinarily contain service-level provisions, under which deficient service results in:

options.A: Deductions or penalties from the payments due to the service provider, as stipulated for the deficiency
options.B: Automatic enhancement of the rates payable to the provider
options.C: Termination of the buyer's registration on the portal
options.D: Forfeiture of the earnest money of all the bidders for the service

q: Materials against which a secured advance has been paid to a works contractor are required to be kept at the site and, until the advance is recovered:

options.A: They may be removed by the contractor to another work of his at his discretion
options.B: They may be sold by the contractor to meet his other liabilities
options.C: They are not to be removed from the site or used on any other work without the permission of the Railway
options.D: They become the property of the contractor free of all encumbrance

q: An 'interim award' which an arbitral tribunal may make during the pendency of a works dispute is an award:

options.A: Which finally disposes of the whole dispute between the parties
options.B: Which is made only after the final award is set aside by a court
options.C: Which the parties are free to disregard during the proceedings
options.D: Made on some of the matters in dispute, such as amounts admitted to be due, before the final award on the remaining matters is made

q: Where a works contractor, with the consent of the Railway, engages a sub-contractor for a specialised portion of the work, the position regarding liability for that portion is that:

options.A: The original contractor is discharged of all liability for that portion
options.B: The original contractor remains fully responsible and liable to the Railway for the execution of that portion, as for the rest of the work
options.C: The Railway becomes directly liable to pay the sub-contractor for that portion in all cases
options.D: The sub-contractor alone becomes a party to the contract with the Railway

q: E-tenders for works invited through IREPS are opened:

options.A: Electronically at the date and time fixed for opening, through the digital signatures of the authorised officials, the bids remaining encrypted and inaccessible before that time
options.B: Manually from the physical tender boxes kept in the division office
options.C: As and when each bid is submitted by a tenderer
options.D: Only after the tender committee submits its briefing note

q: Departmental materials issued to a works contractor remain in his custody at the site until they are consumed in the work. The risk of loss of such materials by fire or theft while in his custody is dealt with by:

options.A: The Railways bearing the loss in all cases, the materials being departmental property
options.B: Writing off the loss without fixing any responsibility
options.C: Requiring the materials in the contractor's custody to be covered by insurance, or the loss to be made good by the contractor, as provided in the contract
options.D: Recovering the loss from the earnest money of the unsuccessful tenderers

q: An application for setting aside an arbitral award arising out of a works contract may be made to the court within the period prescribed under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, which is:

options.A: Thirty days from the receipt of the award in all cases
options.B: Three months from the date on which the party received the award, extendable by a further limited period on sufficient cause being shown
options.C: One year from the date of the award
options.D: At any time, there being no limitation for such an application

q: At the site of a work where a contractor engages labour in large numbers, the provision of amenities such as drinking water, first-aid facilities and rest shelters for the labour is the responsibility of:

options.A: The Railway's medical department in all cases
options.B: The Labour Commissioner of the area personally
options.C: The tender committee which awarded the work
options.D: The contractor, under the applicable labour welfare provisions and the conditions of contract

q: In the terminology of the Engineering and Financial Codes, 'original works' comprise:

options.A: New constructions and additions or alterations which create a new asset or substantially add to an existing asset, as distinct from repairs and maintenance of existing assets
options.B: Only works executed in the first year of a Five Year Plan
options.C: Works executed departmentally without a contractor
options.D: Repairs carried out for the first time on an asset

q: A copy of the contract documents, including the drawings and specifications of the work, is required to be kept at the site of the work principally so that:

options.A: It can be sold to visitors and subcontractors at the site
options.B: It replaces the Measurement Book for recording measurements
options.C: The contractor can avoid keeping any record in his own office
options.D: The work can be executed and supervised at the site with reference to the actual terms, drawings and specifications governing it

q: Instructions and observations recorded during the inspection of a work by the officers of the Railway are entered at the site in the:

options.A: Contractor's Ledger
options.B: Liability Register
options.C: Site Order Book maintained at the site of the work
options.D: Works Register maintained in the Accounts office

q: Works for converting an existing metre gauge or narrow gauge line to broad gauge are charged under:

options.A: Plan Head 11 — New Lines (Construction)
options.B: Plan Head 14 — Gauge Conversion
options.C: Plan Head 15 — Doubling
options.D: Plan Head 31 — Track Renewals

q: A second line provided alongside an existing single line to increase line capacity is classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 11 — New Lines (Construction)
options.B: Plan Head 21 — Rolling Stock
options.C: Plan Head 15 — Doubling
options.D: Plan Head 16 — Traffic Facilities

q: Yard remodelling and provision of additional loops to improve traffic working are classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 16 — Traffic Facilities
options.B: Plan Head 14 — Gauge Conversion
options.C: Plan Head 32 — Bridge Works
options.D: Plan Head 42 — Workshops including Production Units

q: Expenditure on computerisation works of the Railways is classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 33 — Signalling and Telecommunication Works
options.B: Plan Head 64 — Other Specified Works
options.C: Plan Head 18 — Railway Research
options.D: Plan Head 17 — Computerisation

q: Procurement of locomotives, coaches and wagons is planned under:

options.A: Plan Head 41 — Machinery and Plant
options.B: Plan Head 21 — Rolling Stock
options.C: Plan Head 22 — Leased Assets
options.D: Plan Head 16 — Traffic Facilities

q: The capital component of lease charges payable to IRFC for assets taken on lease is charged to:

options.A: Plan Head 21 — Rolling Stock
options.B: Plan Head 64 — Other Specified Works
options.C: Plan Head 16 — Traffic Facilities
options.D: Plan Head 22 — Leased Assets (Capital Component of Lease Charges)

q: Construction of a bridge across a river on an existing line is classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 32 — Bridge Works
options.B: Plan Head 31 — Track Renewals
options.C: Plan Head 30 — Road Safety Works (ROB/RUB)
options.D: Plan Head 16 — Traffic Facilities

q: Purchase of machinery and plant for a workshop is classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 42 — Workshops including Production Units
options.B: Plan Head 21 — Rolling Stock
options.C: Plan Head 41 — Machinery and Plant
options.D: Plan Head 71 — Stores Suspense

q: Extension of an existing workshop building is classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 41 — Machinery and Plant
options.B: Plan Head 42 — Workshops including Production Units
options.C: Plan Head 51 — Staff Quarters
options.D: Plan Head 32 — Bridge Works

q: Construction of residential quarters for railway staff is classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 51 — Staff Quarters
options.B: Plan Head 52 — Amenities for Staff
options.C: Plan Head 53 — Passenger Amenities
options.D: Plan Head 65 — Training and Human Resource Development

q: Provision of a staff institute and a holiday home for railway employees is classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 53 — Passenger Amenities
options.B: Plan Head 51 — Staff Quarters
options.C: Plan Head 64 — Other Specified Works
options.D: Plan Head 52 — Amenities for Staff

q: Works for providing retiring rooms and improved waiting halls for passengers are classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 52 — Amenities for Staff
options.B: Plan Head 53 — Passenger Amenities
options.C: Plan Head 51 — Staff Quarters
options.D: Plan Head 16 — Traffic Facilities

q: A sanctioned work that does not fall under any specific Plan Head is classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 11 — New Lines (Construction)
options.B: Plan Head 73 — Miscellaneous Advances
options.C: Plan Head 64 — Other Specified Works
options.D: Plan Head 81 — Metropolitan Transport Projects

q: Expenditure on training institutes and human resource development programmes is classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 65 — Training and Human Resource Development
options.B: Plan Head 52 — Amenities for Staff
options.C: Plan Head 17 — Computerisation
options.D: Plan Head 42 — Workshops including Production Units

q: Overhead equipment and power supply installations for electric traction are classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 35 — Railway Electrification
options.B: Plan Head 33 — Signalling and Telecommunication Works
options.C: Plan Head 36 — Other Electrical Works
options.D: Plan Head 37 — Traction Distribution Works

q: Budgetary support under the Capital head proves insufficient for a capacity-augmentation work of the Railways. The fund from which such a capital work may be financed in that situation is:

options.A: The ordinary working expenses head
options.B: The Capital Fund
options.C: The dividend account of General Revenues
options.D: The revenue repairs grant

q: Appropriations out of the revenue surplus of the Railways are made to:

options.A: The borrowings account of IRFC
options.B: General Revenues as dividend
options.C: The Development Fund
options.D: The forfeited deposits account

q: The safety surcharge levied on passenger fares, together with grants received from the Central Road Fund, mainly feeds:

options.A: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: The Railway Safety Fund
options.C: The Pension Fund
options.D: The Capital Fund

q: A sanction accorded to expenditure on a work does not by itself authorise incurring that expenditure unless:

options.A: Funds for the purpose have been allotted in the budget
options.B: The work has been completed and taken over
options.C: The tender for the work has been accepted
options.D: The completion report has been vetted by Finance

q: A heavy rush of expenditure concentrated in March, the closing month of the financial year, is regarded under the General Financial Rules as:

options.A: A sign of efficient utilisation of the grant
options.B: A practice permitted without restriction
options.C: A matter for the Tender Committee to regularise
options.D: A breach of financial propriety

q: At the close of the financial year, an unspent balance of allotment remains with a division. Its position in the following year is that it:

options.A: Is carried forward automatically for use in the next year
options.B: Stands transferred to the Development Fund
options.C: Has lapsed and can be used only against a fresh allotment
options.D: May be spent in April without any sanction

q: Expenditure is incurred by an officer beyond the allotment placed at his disposal and without proper authority. The liability for such irregular expenditure rests:

options.A: Personally on the officer concerned
options.B: On no one, if the work executed is useful
options.C: On the Tender Committee of the work
options.D: On the contractor who executed the work

q: An existing contract is extinguished and replaced by a fresh contract with the consent of all the parties concerned. This substitution of contracts is known as:

options.A: Extension of the contract
options.B: Subletting of the contract
options.C: Levy of damages under the contract
options.D: Novation of the contract

q: Execution of a work departmentally, by departmental labour and resources, is ordinarily resorted to when:

options.A: The estimated value of the work is very large
options.B: The work is of an emergent nature, or contractors are not forthcoming for its execution
options.C: The General Manager so desires in every case
options.D: The work requires no material to be procured

q: The rules relating to preparation and sanction of estimates and to tenders and contracts for engineering works are contained in:

options.A: The Indian Railways Works Manual
options.B: The Indian Railways Code for the Engineering Department (Engineering Code)
options.C: The Indian Railways Stores Code
options.D: The Indian Railways Commercial Manual

q: The programme document presented with the Railway Budget, listing the works, machinery and rolling stock programmes, is formally called the:

options.A: Works, Machinery and Rolling Stock Programme of the Railways
options.B: List of Demands for Grants of the Railways
options.C: Appropriation Accounts of the Railways
options.D: Report of the Railway Convention Committee

q: Part II of the Pink Book, i.e. the List of Approved Works, contains works sanctioned by:

options.A: The Railway Board only
options.B: The Divisional Railway Manager only
options.C: The General Manager under his delegated powers
options.D: The Ministry of Finance

q: Sanctions accorded by competent authorities to estimates and expenditure are recorded, for internal check, in a register maintained in the Accounts office known as the:

options.A: Register of Sanctions
options.B: Works Register
options.C: Liability Register
options.D: Contractor's Ledger

q: Under the terminology of the General Financial Rules, the earnest money furnished by a bidder along with his bid is called:

options.A: Performance security
options.B: Bid security
options.C: Retention money
options.D: Tender deposit

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. No interest is payable by the Railways on earnest money and security deposit for the period they are held.
2. Deposits remaining unclaimed for more than three years after they have become refundable are credited to the revenues of the Railways as lapsed deposits.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Booking the cost of a wholly new asset, created where no asset existed earlier, is done on Additional Account.
2. Booking the cost of renewing or replacing an existing asset is done on Replacement Account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Market borrowings are the main source from which the Depreciation Reserve Fund is built up.
2. The Depreciation Reserve Fund receives appropriations from revenue, fixed with reference to the renewals and replacements falling due.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2
